summary: Repository set up from the project brief: knowledge base, data files and dashboard created.
Dashboard redesigned to be easier to follow: this week's jobs up front, plain-English reasons for each job, must-have checklists, and jargon explained on tap.
Added Sky Barrage, a SmartMotion arcade game with 20 levels, in a new Games section of the dashboard.
Added the Print & Design workspace: a 3D model library with 3D views, downloads (STL + STEP), print settings and lessons. Three starter models for the rig: button box, cable clip and VR headset hook.
Dashboard rebuilt as a website for Cloudflare Pages: app icon and phone home-screen support, normal file downloads, and a build that checks the data before every deploy.
Version 1.1.0: the dashboard now shows whether you're signed in (and warns in red if the website has no login protection), and shows its version number under the logo.

Version 1.2.0: new game SmartMotion Flight, a flight simulator-style game around Duxford with SmartMotion signs, a trainer and a WW2 fighter, a gate race, phone, laptop and Meta Quest (VR) support, and motion telemetry for the simulator rig.

Version 1.3.0: SmartMotion Flight now also exists as a native Windows game (built with the Godot engine) that uses the PC's graphics card, with Meta Quest 3 VR over Link and a direct UDP link to the motion rig. It is built automatically and published as a download.

Version 1.4.0: Sam flew the native game in VR on the Quest 3 for the first time; it worked but was hard to control. Flying is now easier (Easy mode sets full power on the runway, power keys respond three times faster, WASD flies in VR too, the right trigger adds power on the Quest controller) and the graphics are better (puffy clouds, a richer sky, proper trees across the countryside, more ground detail, softer light and shadows).

Version 1.5.0: the native SmartMotion Flight game now flies over the real Duxford area, built from free open data: real ground heights (Copernicus DEM), a real satellite photo of the ground (Copernicus Sentinel-2), 129,000 real buildings including the Duxford hangars (Overture Maps / OpenStreetMap), real woods (ESA WorldCover) with trees streamed in as you fly, close-up ground and building textures (ambientCG, free for any use), and 3D clouds you can fly through with shadows on the ground. The runway now has its real heading (058) and length. Credits and licences are recorded (LIC-10 to LIC-14).

Version 1.6.0: you now fly Skysmart's own Scottish Aviation Bulldog (G-SMAT, ex-RAF XX658) in the native game, built from the real dimensions and performance figures, in RAF trainer colours, with a detailed 3D cockpit for VR: live round gauges behind glass, moving control sticks, pedals and levers, seats, canopy frames and an instructor in the right-hand seat. The paint is an assumption until we have photos of the aircraft as it is now.

Version 1.6.1, ready for the VR test: a menu inside the headset (X opens it; stick and A to choose) to change aircraft, start, mode, time of day and Easy/Pro, recentre or leave VR, so no keyboard is needed. Fixed: the controllers didn't work while paused or after a crash (X paused but couldn't resume), and STALL/PULL UP warnings stayed in the headset. VR is also sharper when you turn your head.

Version 1.6.2: smoother flying (buildings and trees now load in the background, so no more stutters when new scenery appears), sharper shadows in the cockpit, a lighter instrument panel, and a cleaner cockpit view on the laptop screen. New automatic check for the scenery loading.

Version 1.6.3: smoother VR. Looking around in the headset stuttered because the game couldn't keep up with the headset. Now the instrument panel's fixed parts are drawn once instead of every frame, shadows in VR are simpler and shorter-range, the picture edges are drawn in less detail (foveated rendering), anti-aliasing is 2x instead of 4x in VR, the headset is asked for a steady 72 Hz (changeable in the in-headset menu, which also shows the frame rate), Quest Link gets depth information so late frames don't warp the cockpit, and scenery loading is spread over more frames. The diagnostics log now records frame timing in VR.

Version 1.6.4: fixes VR not starting in 1.6.3 (the headset stayed on Quest Link's loading hourglass). Foveated rendering, sending depth to the headset and the automatic 72 Hz request are taken out again; the smoother instrument panel, lighter VR shadows, 2x anti-aliasing and spread-out scenery loading stay. The refresh rate can still be changed from the in-headset menu.

Version 1.7.0: in VR you now sit firmly in the seat (the headset was placed one frame behind the aircraft, so the cockpit wobbled around your head in flight), you have gloved hands instead of orange blocks (the right hand closes around the control stick and moves with it, the left takes the throttle), and the game lowers the picture resolution a little by itself whenever the graphics card can't keep up, so it stays smooth.

Version 1.7.1: the Games tile for SmartMotion Flight now gives the Windows download (always the latest) with step-by-step instructions, and explains that you can simply ask Claude in a Claude Code session for the latest link. The browser version of the game is no longer on the website.
Parked idea added: a VR model viewer that turns a 2D component drawing into a 3D model you can inspect at real size in your room.

Version 1.8.0: SmartMotion Flight is now three games in one program, picked at the top of the menu. Racing: drive an open-wheel racing car in SmartMotion colours round a new 4 km circuit with kerbs, gravel, SmartMotion barrier boards, grandstands with crowds, pits and start lights; race seven computer cars over 3 laps or set a fast lap on your own. Space: fly a space fighter round a space station, an asteroid field, a ringed planet and a moon, and shoot down waves of drones. In VR the game's own menus now float in front of you (point and pull the trigger to click), so you can change game and settings without taking the headset off. Both new games drive the motion rig too.

Version 1.9.0: SmartMotion Motion, our own motion program that replaces FlyPT Mover. It is in the same Windows download as the game and works with all three games (Flight, Racing, Space). It reads the game, works out the seat movement and drives the Motion4Sim controller over USB (or the network cable). It has a dry run with a 3D picture of the rig, test movement, safety limits and an emergency stop. In VR the game now cancels the rig's movement out of the headset view. Not yet tried on the real rig (P-10).

Version 1.10.0: the game now starts by asking how the simulator is set up today: flight stick (Flight and Space games), steering wheel (Racing), hands-free ride (the new Roller coaster) or laptop/gamepad (everything). The menu then shows only the games that suit it. New fourth game: a roller coaster beside Duxford airfield with a 52 m lift hill, a drop to 104 km/h, airtime hills and a helix (forces up to about 3 g). New 'Set up controls' screen learns the simulator's own joystick, throttle, pedals or steering wheel by asking you to move each one.

Version 1.11.0: FlyPT Mover can now read our game. The game answers on the network the way X-Plane 11 does, so Mover's ready-made 'X-Plane 11 (UDP)' source picks it up (Flight, Racing, Space and Coaster) and Mover's 3D rig picture moves with the game. Settings > FlyPT Mover, on by default. Steps in the README inside the download.

Version 1.11.1: pressing T now shows a clear message (data panel on or off, and whether FlyPT Mover is reading the game). The game also says 'FlyPT Mover connected' on screen and in VR as soon as Mover starts reading it. Settings has boxes to change the FlyPT ports.

Version 1.11.2: a MOVER light in the cockpit shows the FlyPT Mover link at a glance: dark when off, amber while waiting for Mover, green once Mover is reading the game (Bulldog warning-light row; on the fighter's engine dial).

Version 1.11.3: fixes FlyPT Mover staying on 'waiting'. Like real X-Plane, the game now announces itself on the network once a second so Mover can find it, and it answers Mover's requests on the PC's network address, not only on 127.0.0.1. Windows may ask once to allow the game on networks: allow it.

Version 1.11.4: the game remembers FlyPT Mover. Mover asks for data only once, when it connects; the game now saves that and carries on sending after it restarts (including switching to VR), so Mover doesn't need reconnecting each time.

Version 1.11.5: better FlyPT Mover data for the racing car: engine speed and a rumble on kerbs, gravel and grass. Mover switches to its GROUND pose by itself in the car game (Flight, Space and Coaster use AIR); the README in the download says how to set up the GROUND pose for the car.

Version 1.11.6: fixes a false sideways jolt in the racing car's motion data when moving at walking pace while steering (it read 1.6 g, now near 0). Mover tip in the README: the car's forces are much bigger than the aircraft's, so give the GROUND pose a bigger Range.

Version 1.11.7: VR menus click every time: the trigger (index finger) clicks the moment it goes down, with a short buzz, so a small hand wobble can't make it miss. Better seats in VR and the cockpit view: the racing car's eye point is higher so you see over the halo and the road isn't at your chin; on the roller coaster you now sit in the front seat instead of behind the seat back; in the WW2 fighter the still propeller blade no longer stands in the middle of the windscreen and the stick sits lower so the instruments are clear.

Version 1.12.0: one world. The racing circuit now sits on real farmland 2.5 km west of Duxford runway and the roller coaster just south-east of it; in Flight you can fly over both, exactly as they are in their games. Switching games no longer swaps whole worlds (the likely cause of the occasional crash going from Racing to Flight), and the game keeps the last run's log so a crash can be traced with 'Copy diagnostics'. VR menu: the panel is now big enough for the whole menu, so Settings and Controls always click. Roller coaster: no support post stands in the way of the track any more (the train used to pass through one near the helix), plus two new big sections: a 32 m hill where you float out of your seat and a high banked turn at 25 m that dives back to the ground.

Version 1.13.0: graphics upgrade. Flight: the grey roof smudges in the satellite photo are painted over where the 3D buildings stand (the buildings themselves were already in the right place), the ground is sharper and smoother up close with patches of colour and tractor tracks in the fields, trees have leaf clumps, light through the leaves and sway in the wind, window glass reflects the sky and walls and roofs are weathered. New settings: an Ultra quality (further view, more trees, sharper shadows, reflections), View distance (Near/Normal/Far) and 3D clouds On/Off. Racing and the coaster share the improved world.

Version 1.13.1: joystick left/right (roll, and steering in Racing) and rudder can now be set to Inverted in Settings, like pitch already could. They change the joystick, wheel and gamepad only, not the keyboard or the VR controllers.

Version 1.14.0: graphics overhaul. A physical sky (the colours come from how sunlight scatters in the air, so the sky, haze, sunlight and clouds always match), four times of day (Morning, Midday, Golden hour, Sunset) and a new Weather choice (Clear, Few clouds, Scattered, Broken, Overcast). The aircraft and buildings now go into the shadow of a cloud with the ground, the 3D clouds are lit more like real cumulus, hills and valleys are shaded properly to the horizon, and there is 3D grass round you on the ground. Film-like colour (AgX), sharper textures at low angles, no banding in the sky. New settings: Smooth edges and resolution (TAA, SMAA, FSR 2 Native/Quality/Fast for more frames), 3D grass, Brightness, V-Sync and a frames-per-second counter. Frame rates on Sam's RTX 4060 still to check.

Version 1.14.1: fix for the game crashing when switching between games (for example from the roller coaster to Flight). The game used to throw the aircraft away and build a new one every time Flight came up, including its live instrument screen, and destroying that screen while the graphics card was still using it is the likely cause. Each aircraft is now built once and kept, so nothing is destroyed when you switch. Each switch is also written to the log in case it ever happens again. Needs checking on Sam's PC and in the headset.

Version 1.15.0: real UK detail round Duxford, from free government data (Open Government Licence, credit only). An 8 km square round the airfield now has the Environment Agency's laser-scanned ground heights every 2 m, 44,000 real trees and hedgerow trees where they really stand at their real height, Ordnance Survey roads, water and building outlines drawn sharp, and a 1 m ground picture. The game now opens full screen with a new full-screen loading screen, and the menu has a new layout: the games along the top, options on the left, and a launch panel that says what you've picked. Frame rates and the look need checking on Sam's PC.

Version 1.16.0: the Space game is now a spaceship you can fly everywhere. Start on Duxford's runway (or in space): the ship lifts straight up, hovers, and flies like a fast jet; climb above 20 km and you're in space, above the Earth. Nine places to visit (Earth, the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn with the space station, Uranus, Neptune) with a hyperspeed jump between them (stars stretch into streaks, a flash, a tunnel of light), x10 speed, and flying back down into the Earth's air brings you home over Duxford (TO EARTH does it all on autopilot and lands you). The cockpit has eight lit buttons you press with a fingertip in VR by leaning forward, and screens with speed, height, where you are and the chosen planet. Easy keeps you off the ground and lines you up for hyperspeed. The drone battle is still there as an option. The button reach and hyperspeed in the headset need Sam to try.

Version 1.17.0: smoother VR (the ground's shading is much cheaper, and reflections, wide glow, the big shadow map and half the 3D grass are off in the headset), real-looking vehicles (lacquered paint with panel seams and rivets, carbon fibre, brushed metal, tyre rubber, leather seats and clearer glass, using free public-domain ambientCG textures), towns that look built up instead of grassy fields and every road drawn at its real width with pavements in towns and white road markings round Duxford (Ordnance Survey open data), and in VR the spaceship now flies where you point the right controller while holding the grip. VR frame rate to check on Sam's Quest.

Version 1.17.1: a real horizon at every height. The game now draws 600 km (it stopped at 40 km, so the ground ended at an edge that moved as you climbed), the ground follows the curve of the Earth out to about 1,000 km, far-away hills no longer pop as you fly, and the land beyond the real 32 km map levels out instead of repeating hills.

Version 1.18.0: the Bulldog now looks like G-SMAT in Sam's photos and video (light grey panel with the real placards, light grey sticks with white grips, red cowling and lower fuselage, silver wings with red outer panels, black-and-white propeller). VR hands are now small balls at the controllers in every game. In space, HYPERSPEED goes to the planet you are looking at. The game always opens on Flight. Going from Space to Flight now changes worlds a step at a time (likely cause of the crash), with each step logged.

Version 1.19.0 of the game: trim up and down while flying (hold ] or [; it now works in Easy mode too); the four stray buildings on the runway are gone; every key can be changed in Settings (two keys and one controller button per control, trim included); the Controls screen is now a picture of the keyboard with each key labelled; F1 shows the controls while playing; in VR you can no longer lean out of the seat; and the Bulldog's cockpit was rebuilt to fit (panel, glare shield, walls, seats and propeller no longer poke through the fuselage or canopy).

New FlyPT Mover profile for the games (SmartMotion-Games.Mover, in the Windows download from version 1.19.1): made from Sam's own profile, with smooth filters on every movement and limits that keep every actuator inside its 300 mm travel. The old profile slammed heave between its limits, moved the rig twice over in the air and could ask actuators for nearly twice their travel. Checked by replaying each game's recorded data through a model of Mover; not yet tried on the rig.
